title: Smooth centralizers of split diagonalizable subgroups over rings
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $N$ a finitely generated abelian group. Put $K=D_R(N)=\operatorname{Spec}R[N]$ with the group operations of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Let $G$ be a smooth affine $S$-group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $j:K\hookrightarrow G$ be a homomorphism which is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. An $S$-group scheme here has multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams, as in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. For a commutative $R$-algebra $B$ define $C(B)$ to consist of $g\in G(B)$ whose image commutes with $j(k)$ for every commutative $B$-algebra $B'$ and every $k\in K(B')$. Then $C$ is represented by a smooth affine $S$-group scheme of finite presentation, closed in $G$. For every commutative $R$-algebra $R'$ its base change $C_{R'}$ represents the centralizer of $K_{R'}$ in $G_{R'}$. For any commutative $R$-algebra $B$, put $\operatorname{Lie}(G_B)=\ker(G(B[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to G(B))$ and define $\operatorname{Lie}(C_B)$ similarly, with their usual $B$-module structures. Under the inclusion into $\operatorname{Lie}(G_B)$, one has $\operatorname{Lie}(C_B)=\operatorname{Lie}(G_B)^{K_B}$, where invariance means fixed by the full conjugation action after every $B$-algebra extension, rather than by its differential. These equalities and inclusions are natural under further scalar extension. The assertions allow torsion in $N$, nonreduced $R$ and $R'$, and $N=0$; neither $K$ nor $C$ is required to have connected fibres.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Lemma 2.2.4 and proof, printed pp.64--66; arbitrary base change follows from the universal centralizer functor. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states the smooth diagonalizable-centralizer theorem.

proof.text:
Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], $A$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra. Conjugation by $j$ is the action $\alpha:K\times_SG\to G$, $(k,g)\mapsto j(k)gj(k)^{-1}$. Using [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the basis $e_n$ of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group], uniquely expand
$$\alpha^*(a)-1\otimes a=\sum_{n\in N}e_n\otimes d_n(a)\quad(a\in A),$$
with finite support for each $a$. Let $I\subseteq A$ be the ideal generated by all $d_n(a)$ and set $Q=A/I$. For an $R$-algebra $B$ and $g:A\to B$, the map $\operatorname{id}_{B[N]}:B[N]\to B[N]$ is the universal $K_B$-point. Its conjugation fixes $g$ exactly when $\sum_ne_n\otimes g(d_n(a))=0$ for all $a$, equivalently $g(I)=0$ by uniqueness of coefficients. Every $k\in K(B')$ is an evaluation of this universal point, so this is equivalent to all the commutation equations in $C(B)$. Conversely that condition includes the universal point with $B'=B[N]$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-alg}}(Q,B)=C(B)$, naturally in $B$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.4, representability assertion, printed pp.64–65; explicit free-coordinate alternative to its torsion-level intersections (cf. Remark 2.2.7).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion], $C=\operatorname{Spec}Q$ is a closed affine subscheme of $G$. For every test algebra, $C(B)$ is a subgroup: two elements commuting with every $j(k)$ have a commuting product and inverse, and the identity commutes. These pointwise formulas restrict the multiplication, identity and inverse of $G$ to $C$, and the group diagrams restrict with them by the affine-spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $A$ is finitely generated over $R$, so is its quotient $Q$; $R$ is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes $Q$ finitely presented over $R$. Its finite polynomial presentation is precisely finite presentation of this affine $S$-scheme. No finiteness of the character set is used in forming $I$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.4, representability and finite presentation; Stacks 01IG, schemes.tex example-closed-immersion-affines; 00FP, algebra.tex lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation.

proof.text: For any $R\to R'$ and any $R'$-algebra $B$, the affine fibre-product description [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $C_{R'}(B)=C(B)$ and $G_{R'}(B)=G(B)$. Moreover $R'[N]=R'\otimes_RR[N]$, by sending $r'\otimes e_n$ to $r'e_n$, so $K_{R'}(B')=K(B')$ for every $B$-algebra $B'$. The commutation condition is therefore exactly the same condition on both sides. This proves the asserted base-change representability, including nonflat $R'$; it uses no assertion that kernels of arbitrary module maps commute with tensor products.

source.place: Definition 2.2.1 and universal centralizer functor, printed p.64; free-coordinate construction of step 1.

proof.text: Let $D$ be any commutative $R$-algebra, $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, and $c_0\in C(D/J)$. Smoothness of $G$ in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] supplies $g\in G(D)$ lifting $c_0$. Put $H=D_D(N)$. The two homomorphisms $f_1=\operatorname{Int}(g)\circ j_D$ and $f_2=j_D$ agree over $D/J$, since $c_0$ centralizes $K_{D/J}$ as a group functor. Apply [lem-sfb-split-diagonalizable-infinitesimal-conjugacy] to get $u\in G(D)$ reducing to $1$ with $\operatorname{Int}(u)f_1=f_2$. Its ambient group $G_D$ is affine and finitely presented: tensor the finite polynomial presentation of $A$ in step 1 with $D$. It is smooth because a lifting problem for $G_D$ is a lifting problem for $G$ with the given $D$-structure on the affine test thickening; the lift paired with that structure lands in $G_D$. Now $\operatorname{Int}(ug)j_D=j_D$, hence $ug\in C(D)$, and $ug$ reduces to $c_0$. Thus $C$ is formally smooth. Together with its finite presentation from step 2, [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] proves it smooth.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.4, smoothness paragraph, printed pp.65–66; use Corollary B.2.6 on the actual homomorphisms, avoiding the extra subgroup-identification step. Stacks 02H6, more-morphisms.tex lemma-smooth-formally-smooth.

proof.text:
Fix an $R$-algebra $B$ and put $B[\epsilon]=B[T]/(T^2)$. Since $C(B[\epsilon])\subseteq G(B[\epsilon])$ and $C(B)\subseteq G(B)$, its Lie module embeds in that of $G$. Apply [lem-sfb-group-space-square-zero-kernel-module] to these split square-zero thickenings for the usual module structures. Let $v\in\operatorname{Lie}(G_B)$ and let $k_{\mathrm{univ}}\in K(B[N])$ correspond to the identity of $B[N]$. By the definition of the conjugation action on Lie vectors, invariance of $v$ implies
$$j(k_{\mathrm{univ}})v_{B[N]}j(k_{\mathrm{univ}})^{-1}=v_{B[N]}\quad\text{in }G(B[N][\epsilon]).$$
The coefficient criterion of step 1, now for the point $v\in G(B[\epsilon])$ and using $B[N][\epsilon]=B[\epsilon][N]$, says exactly that $v\in C(B[\epsilon])$. Its reduction is the identity, so $v\in\operatorname{Lie}(C_B)$. Conversely a point of $C(B[\epsilon])$ commutes with every constant $k\in K(B')$ in $G(B'[\epsilon])$ for every $B$-algebra $B'$, giving invariance. These are equal submodules: multiplication of infinitesimal points is addition, and scaling is induced by $\epsilon\mapsto b\epsilon$; both preserve the same commutation equations. For $B\to B_1$, the ring map $B[\epsilon]\to B_1[\epsilon]$ respects reduction, group operations, these scaling maps, and conjugation. It therefore takes this equality and its inclusion into the corresponding equality and inclusion over $B_1$, giving the asserted naturality. The argument uses the universal group point, so remains valid for nonsmooth $K$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.4, Lie-invariant conclusion, printed p.66; direct dual-number and universal-point verification, without reducing invariance to the differential action.
